stem.en: Meera says, 'The poles are cold because they are far from the Sun.' Which is the best reply?

text.en: She is right, because the poles are thousands of km further from the Sun.

feedback.en: They are further, but a few thousand km is tiny next to 15 crore km.

text.en: She has it backwards, because the poles are nearer to the Sun.

feedback.en: The equator is slightly nearer to the Sun, not the poles.

text.en: Neither distance nor angle matters, because only cloud decides temperature.

feedback.en: Cloud matters on a given day, but the angle of sunlight sets the pattern from equator to pole.

text.en: The extra distance is tiny next to 15 crore km; slanting sunlight spreading out matters far more.

feedback.en: Yes. The difference in distance is far too small, while the angle changes a lot.

explanation.en: The Sun is about 15 crore km away, so a few thousand km more makes almost no difference. Near the poles sunlight arrives at a low angle and spreads over a wider area, so less energy reaches each part of the ground.

hints.en: Compare a few thousand km with 15 crore km.
What changes more from equator to pole: the distance or the angle of the sunlight?
